claim: The new `reportDiagnostic` wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of this compilation, including Location.None. That covers the many diagnostics built from helpers that return null, such as GetIdentifierLocation, GetLocation and GetParameterListLocation. Before the change, a diagnostic about a type declared in the compiling assembly whose helper returned null was still reported with no location. Now it is silently discarded. This goes beyond 'do not crash on metadata symbols' and can contradict 'types declared in the same assembly keep working as before'.

claim: The new reporter wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of this compilation, including Location.None. Location.None is legal for analyzers; only locations in foreign trees are forbidden. The change also turns the field-loop MemberNeedsKey location into `FirstOrDefault()` (possibly null). Together these mean a source-declared [MessagePackObject] type in this compilation can now silently lose a diagnostic. Example: a public field without [Key] inherited from a base class in a referenced assembly. `formattedType` has syntax, so the new guard passes, but `item` has none, so the location is Location.None and the wrapper drops it. Any other diagnostic built with the null-returning helpers (GetParameterListLocation for an implicit constructor, GetLocation(parameter)) on a source type is dropped the same way. L8 covers types from referenced assemblies, not source types that inherit from them.
